plant.cvs: 'Kramer's Rote' – magenta flowers, bronze-green foliage · 'White Perfection' – white flowers, bright green foliage · 'Darley Dale' – pale pink, the original hybrid · 'Silberschmelze' – white, scented
plant.foliage: evergreen; fine needle-like golden-yellow leaves, orange-red tips on new growth
plant.hardinessNote: Very hardy throughout the UK, tolerating temperatures below -20°C.
plant.pollination: not applicable; grown for flowers and foliage
plant.prune: Trim lightly with shears straight after flowering to remove spent spikes and keep it compact. Do not cut into bare old wood.
plant.resilience: Very hardy and tolerates lime better than most heathers. Gold foliage colours best in sun and may scorch in hot dry spots. Pests: occasional vine weevil; root rot in wet soil.

peak/hue: peak is set to the flowering season (Dec-Apr), which is when it sells. Exact flowering months are not verified. Hue is set to the gold foliage, which is the year-round dominant feature, rather than the pink flowers.
visual: the orange-red spring tips and lilac-pink flower colour are as remembered, not verified.
toxicity: Erica is not on common UK toxic plant lists as far as I know. Other Ericaceae (Rhododendron, Kalmia) contain grayanotoxins, so confirm online.
compliance: possible plant breeders' rights not known. The breeder is believed to be Kurt Kramer (Germany), not verified.
clay: left blank. Heathers dislike heavy waterlogged clay, but tolerance of improved clay is not established.
sunMin: 50 is a judgement (tolerates light shade but loses gold colour).

plant.uses: Winter containers · rockeries · ground cover · front of border · heather beds
plant.visual: Golden-yellow needle foliage all year · lilac-pink flower spikes Dec-Apr · orange-red new tips in spring
plant.water: Water regularly in the first year and in dry spells; keep pots evenly moist.
